title: Higher-Order Functions
definition: A Higher-Order Function is a function that does at least one of two things: it takes one or more functions as arguments (callbacks), or it returns a function as its result.
simpleExplanation: Think of a higher-order function like a factory manager. Instead of just taking raw materials (numbers, strings), the manager takes IN other workers (callbacks) and tells them when to do their job. Or, the manager might hire a new worker and give them to you (returning a function).
realWorldExample: The `setTimeout` function is a built-in higher-order function. You pass it a function (what to do) and a time (when to do it). It takes your function as an argument and executes it later.
useCases: Array methods like map, filter, and reduce

answers.question: What is a callback function?
answers.answer: A callback is a function passed into another function as an argument, which is then invoked inside the outer function to complete some kind of routine or action.

answers.question: Why are functions considered 'first-class citizens'?
answers.answer: Because functions in JavaScript are treated like any other variable. They can be passed as arguments, returned by other functions, and assigned to variables.

answers.question: What happens if you pass console.log to map? [1,2,3].map(console.log)
answers.answer: It prints the value, the index, and the whole array for each element! Because map passes three arguments to its callback, and console.log accepts infinite arguments.
